candidates.source_title: Rochdale Council rakes in almost £3m from parking fines
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale council has raked in £2.88m from parking fines in the last three years. Data obtained from a Freedom of Information (FOI) request revealed that the local authority has generated just under £1m per year from 2023 to 2026. From a total of 90,644 parking charge notices (PCNs) issued for 2023, 2024 and 2025, the council gained £2.88m, with the highest earning year being 2025 with £990,256. The total value of PCNs was just over £5.6m, but the income is less due to people successfully challenging claims or costs of chasing fines. The town hall says all money generated from PCNs is then reinvested into the road network. This reinvestment could include fixing potholes, re-drawing on road markers or larger infrastructure projects. The local authority also pointed out PCNs are issued for safety reasons, such as making sure pavements have enough space for wheelchair users or to prevent blind spots at junctions. The FOI, submitted by the Local Democracy Reporting Service, also revealed the biggest hotspots in the borough where people get PCNs. Newgate, Yorkshire Street Central and Oldham Road Central were all the places with the highest number of PCNs distributed. Newgate: Number of PCNs – 790, total income: £54,920 Yorkshire St Central: Number of PCNs – 623, total income: £39,970

candidates.source_title: The scheme to regenerate land around Rochdale station progressing
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A scheme which would transform the gateway into Rochdale is making significant progress, town hall bosses say. Some 81 two, three-and four-bedroom homes are currently under construction on vacant land next to Rochdale’s Central Retail Park. This forms part of a wider scheme to create a connection between the train station and the town centre. The wider regeneration of the area around Rochdale railway station also involves the creation of a new public square in front of the station and 33 new apartments on a brownfield site on the corner of Maclure Road and Station Road. The train station in Rochdale was once a hub for industrial business generations ago, so the distance between the station and the town centre was purposeful separation. But as times changed, society changed and the station suddenly started transporting people, not goods. This is why there is an idea to improve access and avenues from the station and the main hub of the town. This 81-home development, known as John Rennie Place, in honour of the late Scottish Civil engineer who masterminded the Rochdale Canal, got under way in November last year, and is due for completion in December 2027. The project, approved years ago, was unlocked following a successful bid for £15m from the government’s Community Regeneration Partnerships Fund. The transformation has been on the cards for a long time, but the local authority struggled to get the investment until last year. The properties will be the first affordable net zero homes delivered as part of a housing scheme supported by the council. The local authority says the development is already delivering benefits to the local economy and community.
candidates.source_summary: A scheme which would transform the gateway into Rochdale is making significant progress, town hall bosses say.

candidates.source_title: The potential return of Lodge Mill
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Lodge Mill in Middleton was devastated by a fire six months ago. Now there is hope for its future thanks to some dedicated business owners, volunteers and one avid ice cream fan. In March, firefighters were called to the massive blaze that left businesses in tatters and left the historic mill a shell. Several businesses were based on the ground floor of the building, believed to be one of the oldest mills in Middleton. A children’s dance studio, an ice cream parlour, a tea room, a dog chiropractor business and the Engine House event space, which held weddings, functions and parties, were all lost in the fire. The former silk and cotton mill, on Townley Street, dates back to around 1850. It was bought by couple Martin Cove and Paula Hickey in 2019, who were working passionately to renovate the three floors above. The pair have since kickstarted a fundraising campaign to restore the building soon after the fire, because the mill was uninsurable. Martin and Paula said the blaze ’caused the almost total loss of the main mill structure’. “No one was injured, and for that we are incredibly thankful,” the couple said at the time of the fire. “But we are heartbroken at the loss of not only our beloved Lodge Mill, but also the homes of the many local businesses and the community space we had all built together. “The outpouring of love and compassion from the people of Middleton and the surrounding area has given us the strength to carry on.” The GoFundMe page has raised just over £7,000 since it was launched six months ago. Thanks to a group of keen volunteers, life has returned to the mill.

candidates.source_title: Major Rochdale housing scheme delayed again over flood concerns
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The decision over the first phase of a 450-home development in Rochdale has been delayed again. In August, Rochdale council ’s planning committee deferred making a decision on Wain Homes’ proposals to build 45 houses on a plot of land behind Greenvale in Bamford. Committee members felt they didn’t have enough detail about how the developers would solve historic drainage issues. Councillors said the lack of a masterplan for the wider scheme prevented them from making a call. The proposal would be the first of many for the former green belt land, which contains a number of playing fields and sports pitches. The site was taken out of the green belt following the adoption of the Greater Manchester housing strategy, Places for Everyone. But when the committee met again to discuss the application on October 22, they felt they didn’t get what they had asked for. Objector Lisa Bailey said the site – to the west of Norden Road – has a history of flooding and is ‘seasonally wet ground’. United Utilities want to see a drainage plan, the Save Bamford Greenbelt group representative explained. She said infrastructure and access issues have not been addressed, adding: “If these documents are still not before you, the reason for your deferral in August has not been addressed. “We know this land will be developed, but it’s about how it will be developed. If we don’t we’ll end up with a piecemeal development.” Coun Stephen Anstee said he’d never seen as many as 18 conditions, including one on drainage, attached to a planning application. He said that demonstrated that scheme is not ready. Planning agent Stephen Harris told the committee a flood risk management assessment was part of the application. He added that the other developers, who would bring forward the rest of the 450 homes, told Wain Homes their scheme would not obstruct the wider scheme. candidates.source_title: Final crossing for popular lollipop lady Barbara - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A popular lollipop lady has helped schoolchildren cross the road for the final time today. Barbara Gould is retiring after looking after youngsters across Middleton for 34 years. Wishing Barbara a happy retirement, Cllr Dylan Williams, Rochdale Council Cabinet Member for Highways and Facilities, shared on Facebook: “I had the pleasure of visiting much-loved lollipop lady/ school crossing patrol officer Barbara Gould, who retires today after 34 years serving our local community since 1992. “Over that time, Barbara has served St Michael’s Primary School / St Thomas More, Alkrington Primary, Middleton Technology School and St Peter’s Primary School in Middleton, keeping lots of children and parents safe crossing the road. “I’m 28 years old and I remember Barbara helping me cross the road when I went to St Michael’s Primary School. “Well done Barbara for your 34 years of service to our local community and I hope you have the best retirement!” Barbara said: “I’ve enjoyed my job tremendously. It’s the joy of getting up and knowing who I will be seeing. The children always have a smile and they speak to me and share their problems. More recently, I’ve had the pleasure of crossing the children of people I crossed when they were at school.” READ MORE: No decision yet on College Bank – but ‘renovation would take more than a decade’

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A Rochdale school has closed after a bomb threat earlier today. Greater Manchester Police were called to St Cuthbert’s RC High School which was placed into lockdown this morning following a call made to the school. A spokesperson for the school said: “The emergency services were called and all school buildings were evacuated as a precautionary measure. candidates.source_body_excerpt: League Two club Rochdale have signed experienced attacking player Jamie Paterson on deal until the end of the season. The 34-year-old, who played second-tier football for Nottingham Forest, Huddersfield, Bristol City, Derby, Swansea and Coventry, was a free agent after being released by League One side Plymouth Argyle at the end of last season. The Manchester United youth product made his senior debut for Walsall in League One in 2010 and was picked up by Forest after impressing for the Saddlers. candidates.source_title: Drivers have vehicles seized for ignoring school crossing patrols - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Two drivers have had their vehicles seized after failing to stop for school crossing patrols and almost knocking them over. Rochdale Council has revealed that the incidents — involving a car and a moped — were among 137 incidents in the past five years in which motorists failed to stop for school crossing patrols, as required by law. The incidents took place on October 13 and 14, with school crossing patrol Barry Jones having to move out of the way to avoid the vehicles, even though he was already standing in the road. The matter was reported to police, who used new powers under section 59 of the police reform act 2002, to seize the vehicles after collecting evidence, including witness statements. Cars and other vehicles failing to stop for school crossing patrols is a growing problem, with 137 fail to stops reported across Rochdale borough over the past five years. Body-worn cameras are now being used in hotspot areas to try to deter dangerous driving and support prosecutions where needed. Cllr Dylan Williams, cabinet member for highways and facilities, said: “It beggars belief that somebody would see a school crossing patrol clearly standing in the middle of the road and continue to drive. Frankly I’m appalled. “We would like to thank GMP for their quick and decisive action and I think it’s a really good result.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Council has raked in £2.88m from parking fines in the last three years. Data obtained from a Freedom of Information (FOI) request revealed that the local authority has generated just under £1m per year from 2023 to 2026. From a total of 90,644 parking charge notices (PCNs) issued for 2023, 2024 and 2025, the council gained £2.88m, with the highest earning year being 2025 with £990,256. The total value of PCNs was just over £5.6m, but the income is less due to people successfully challenging claims or costs of chasing fines. The town hall says all money generated from PCNs is then reinvested into the road network. This reinvestment could include fixing potholes, re-drawing on road markers or larger infrastructure projects. The local authority also pointed out PCNs are issued for safety reasons, such as making sure pavements have enough space for wheelchair users or to prevent blind spots at junctions. The FOI, submitted by the Local Democracy Reporting Service, also revealed the biggest hotspots in the borough where people get PCNs. Newgate, Yorkshire Street Central and Oldham Road Central were all the places with the highest number of PCNs distributed.

"Since receiving the report earlier today, we have been carrying out a number of lines of enquiry but our priority to find the woman and make sure she is safe and well," Detective Daly said. "She may be in need of urgent medical attention, and she is our absolute priority at the moment - that is why we are asking anyone with information to contact us. Information can also be reported online or by using our LiveChat service at www.gmp.police.uk. Alternatively, contact Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111. candidates.source_title: No decision yet on College Bank – but ‘renovation would take more than a decade’ - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Renovating Rochdale’s iconic Seven Sisters tower blocks would force residents out of their homes for more than a decade, housing chiefs have said. While Rochdale Boroughwide Housing says no decision on the future of the landmark College Bank blocks has been taken, residents have asked new Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig to back their campaign to refurbish their homes rather than demolish them. But if campaigners get their wish, the scale of bringing the 61-year-old buildings up to modern standards would take more than 10 years and they could not be occupied until the work is complete, RBH chiefs have said. Members of Greater Manchester Tenants Union recently met Ms Craig to discuss the steps that could be taken to renovate almost 1,000 homes in College Bank and Lower Falinge. Plans to demolish College Bank were first discussed in 2017 when RBH warned that the buildings were approaching the end of their life. Tenants set up the Save the Seven Sisters campaign and hoped RBH’s partnership with Legal and General Affordable Homes would see the towers restored. But in September, 2024, it was announced that the partnership would not continue. The union and the Save the Seven Sisters campaign asked then Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham to help. In November, 2024, the Mayoral Taskforce was established to look at the options for the College Bank estate. Rochdale’s skyline without the Seven Sisters towers. Image: Copilot In October 2025, RBH announced the results of surveys which found the blocks were not safe to remain occupied and residents would be required to leave their homes.

candidates.source_title: Two days that will decide the future of Hopwood Hall - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The battle for Hopwood Hall returns to the courtroom today with ownership of the historic manor house at stake. Hopwood DePree and Rochdale Council begin a two-day trial in the High Court in Manchester later over Mr DePree’s bid to restore his ancestral home. Mr DePree is a descendant of the Hopwood family which build the manor house in the 1420s. The family owned the hall and surrounding land — which is now Hopwood Hall College — until 1922. The house was sold 20 years later. It was occupied by a variety of temporary residents, including the de la Salle Brothers, who ran it as a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s. It had fallen into disrepair and was bought by Rochdale Council, which still owns the Grade II-listed property. The legal action initiated by Mr DePree was launched after he spent seven years working with the council to carry out vital repairs on the dilapidated site with a view to purchasing it. In November, 2024, the council ended its exclusivity agreement with Mr DePree, and said it would explore other options because no “commercially viable” business model had been presented. READ MORE: Four arrests and £1m drugs seizure in Rochdale Mr DePree’s case is that the council went back on his option to purchase Hopwood Hall upon planning permission being granted in 2022. His claim is that the agreement triggers have been satisfied and the council must proceed with the ownership transfer.

candidates.source_title: 'We were outstanding and should have won the game' - David Artell's verdict on Rochdale draw - Grimsby Live
candidates.source_body_excerpt: David Artell had all too familiar feelings after Grimsby Town’s 2-2 draw away at Rochdale, with the result not matching the performance in his eyes. The Mariners snapped their four-game losing streak in the league at least, but Artell felt they deserved all three points, praising the character of his side amidst a poor run of results and a growing injury list. Town were behind at the break despite a solid first half showing, but Kieran Green’s fourth goal of the campaign and a first for Jamie Walker put them in front with less than 20 minutes left on the clock. They could have gone further ahead before Ian Henderson restored parity in the 88th minute, with more ‘what if’ moments to reflect on for Town on Tuesday night in a season that has already been packed with them. Artell said: “We were outstanding and should have won the game. It probably summed up our season so far – we should have won comfortably, having shown outstanding character – the run we’ve been on, the injury list. “We should be sitting here with three points, and it would be no more than we deserved. We should have won against Northampton on Saturday, and we were even better tonight. The fans knew that, nearly a thousand travelling supporters applauded us off at the end. “We were magnificent. We had lots of gilt-edged chances, and their only threat was in transition and through Aden Flint from set-pieces, and we coped well with that. “We dominated the first half and shouldn’t have been a goal down at half-time. We said to them at the break, let’s see what we’re made of, and we kept going to the well.” How much a draw will do to lift the mood in the camp remains to be seen, but the performance did show a team that are fighting even if their imperfections are clear to see. It is hard for Artell not to feel as though Mother Nature is currently working against him and his team, with the pile-up of defensive injuries and certain moments in games that are snatching victories away from them. “It’s always important,” explained the Mariners boss on stopping the losing streak. “We came out and played even better in the second half after controlling the first, so the character the team showed in the face of quite a lot of adversity is commendable. “We were the better team for most of the game, but unfortunately again we haven’t quite managed to get over the line. We had a chance to go 3-1 up and not quite taken it, and it seems like things like that are going against us at the moment. “Their lad has gone in on Jamie Walker, who has evidence all over his shin, it’s as clear as day, second yellow card, and the ref didn’t even think it was a foul, so it’s little things like that going against us. “I don’t want fans to think I’m moaning because I don't talk about injuries even though we’ve got a bus-load of them.” Town are in the middle of a pack of teams that could still go either way in a League Two table that is far from set, but Artell falls back again on the underlying numbers that he believes show his team are inches away from shooting upwards again. He concluded: “I can’t let the pressure get to me because that feeds into the team. The pressure is always there in every game, but I know how good we are. I got sent an expected points table, and we’re third in it. “Fans will think I’m chatting a load of baloney, but I’ve been doing this for nearly eight years now, so I know when we’re miles off it and know when we’re close.”

candidates.source_title: Here’s what a major housing scheme in Rochdale could look like according to new plans - I Love Manchester
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Seven blocks on Rochdale’s Lower Falinge estate are set to be demolished to make way for 270 new homes . Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) have officially submitted plans to the council to bulldoze Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, Zedburgh and Vaynor. Once they are demolished RBH would start work on building a mixture of homes and flats, all available for social rent. The majority of the 270 homes would go on the land due to be bulldozed – next to Sheriff Street and Falinge Road to the west. There are plots east of the giant estate, near to Redcross Street, that would also be built on under the proposals. RBH bought up the land to the east in recent years, just next to St Mary’s Gate. The proposals, if approved by Rochdale council, also intend to create new landscaping, public open spaces, safer streets, and new walking routes into the town centre. RBH says they have to demolish the seven remaining blocks because they are at the end of their life and no longer provide safe, warm homes. Six of the blocks have been empty for years. Only Zedburgh remains occupied by Andy Roche and his partner.

candidates.source_title: Ian Watson lauds ‘amazing’ Ian Henderson after late Rochdale leveller - Peeblesshire News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Manager Ian Watson hailed ‘amazing’ Ian Henderson after the 41-year-old striker rescued a point for Rochdale in a 2-2 draw against Grimsby at the Crown Oil Arena. Henderson came off the bench in the 81st minute with Dale trailing 2-1 and was in the right place to turn home Charlie Tasker’s delivery seven minutes later to secure a share of the spoils. Watson said: “It was a really hard game. I’d said to the boys beforehand that we were up against a really good side with a really good manager in David Artell. “They have a really aggressive way of playing off the ball and it wasn’t just from restarts, it was man v man for most of the game. In those moments we have to be good with the ball and I thought we could have been a bit braver but it is really hard against such an aggressive opponent. “It was a game that ebbed and flowed, we had the momentum, then they had it. We spoke to the lads at half-time about what we needed to improve on but we weren’t able to carry any momentum from that first half into the second and they came out a bit better than us. “But even when we conceded the second goal I felt there was something in it for us and I don’t even have any words for Ian Henderson, he’s an amazing guy and an amazing footballer.” Dale took the lead in the 38th minute when Glenn Middleton crossed for Dajaune Brown to slide home the opener. But the Mariners, on the back of a four-game losing streak, turned the game on its head with Kieran Green levelling in the 57th minute and Jamie Walker firing them ahead 15 minutes later.

candidates.source_title: Substitute Ian Henderson rescues Rochdale point against Grimsby - Peeblesshire News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Veteran striker Ian Henderson came off the bench to rescue a point for Rochdale with an 88th-minute leveller as they drew 2-2 with Grimsby. The 41-year-old converted Charlie Tasker’s cross from close range at the end of a high-octane clash at the Crown Oil Arena. The home side made the brighter start, Glenn Middleton’s shot being cleared off the line by Joe Foulkes. Grimsby’s best effort of the half came from Charles Vernam, a fierce shot saved by Dale goalkeeper Sam Waller. Rochdale took the lead in the 38th minute when Middleton got in behind the Mariners’ backline and fired an inviting cross to the back post where Dajaune Brown slid in and side-footed home. Grimsby levelled in the 57th minute, Harvey Rodgers’ delivery to the back post picking out Andy Cook and though Waller saved his header, Kieran Green was there to nod home. The visitors took the lead in the 72nd minute when Jamie Walker collected a partially-cleared corner and slammed a low shot through a crowded penalty, but Henderson denied the Mariners victory with a poacher’s finish.

candidates.source_title: Substitute Ian Henderson rescues Rochdale point against Grimsby - Border Telegraph
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Veteran striker Ian Henderson came off the bench to rescue a point for Rochdale with an 88th-minute leveller as they drew 2-2 with Grimsby. The 41-year-old converted Charlie Tasker’s cross from close range at the end of a high-octane clash at the Crown Oil Arena. The home side made the brighter start, Glenn Middleton’s shot being cleared off the line by Joe Foulkes. Grimsby’s best effort of the half came from Charles Vernam, a fierce shot saved by Dale goalkeeper Sam Waller. Rochdale took the lead in the 38th minute when Middleton got in behind the Mariners’ backline and fired an inviting cross to the back post where Dajaune Brown slid in and side-footed home. Grimsby levelled in the 57th minute, Harvey Rodgers’ delivery to the back post picking out Andy Cook and though Waller saved his header, Kieran Green was there to nod home. The visitors took the lead in the 72nd minute when Jamie Walker collected a partially-cleared corner and slammed a low shot through a crowded penalty, but Henderson denied the Mariners victory with a poacher’s finish.

The 41-year-old converted Charlie Tasker’s cross from close range at the end of a high-octane clash at the Crown Oil Arena. The home side made the brighter start, Glenn Middleton’s shot being cleared off the line by Joe Foulkes. Grimsby’s best effort of the half came from Charles Vernam, a fierce shot saved by Dale goalkeeper Sam Waller. Rochdale took the lead in the 38th minute when Middleton got in behind the Mariners’ backline and fired an inviting cross to the back post where Dajaune Brown slid in and side-footed home. Grimsby levelled in the 57th minute, Harvey Rodgers’ delivery to the back post picking out Andy Cook and though Waller saved his header, Kieran Green was there to nod home. The visitors took the lead in the 72nd minute when Jamie Walker collected a partially-cleared corner and slammed a low shot through a crowded penalty, but Henderson denied the Mariners victory with a poacher’s finish.
candidates.source_summary: The 41-year-old ensured a share of the spoils at the Crown Oil Arena with late leveller.

candidates.source_title: Greater Manchester schools receive 750,600 fruit and veg portions through Tesco scheme
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Schools across Greater Manchester, including Rochdale, received 750,600 portions of fruit and vegetables during the second year of Tesco’s Free Fruit & Veg for Schools programme. The produce weighed more than 60,000kg and was distributed through the programme, which Tesco developed in partnership with the British Nutrition Foundation. Apples were the most popular choice among participating Greater Manchester schools, accounting for around 221,000 portions. Bananas followed with around 103,000 portions, ahead of satsumas and clementines with around 88,000. Schools in Rochdale received a share of the regional total, although a separate figure for the borough was not provided. Tesco said almost 20 million portions had been eaten through the programme across the UK during its first two years, reaching up to 186,000 pupils. Now in its third year, the scheme has expanded to support more than 1,000 schools. According to the programme’s impact report, 98% of teachers surveyed said it encouraged pupils to eat a wider variety of fruit, while 94% reported improved behaviour. More than 1,500 tonnes of produce have been provided since the programme began, with pupils trying 103 types of fruit and vegetables.

candidates.source_title: New bid for extra trains from Rochdale to London is refused - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to improve the rail link between Rochdale and London have hit the buffers again. Today, the Office of Rail and Road announced it had rejected proposals for new train services which would have seen Lumo operate up to four additional return Rochdale-to-Euston services on weekdays and Saturdays and three services on Sundays . Among those backing calls for the extra services was Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, who called Lumo’s bid to restore six daily direct services between Rochdale and the capital a “game-changing opportunity” for the borough and the wider North West. But the ORR rejected the plans after its assessment found adding more trains to the West Coast Main Line — which also included services to Blackpool and Wrexham — would likely increase delays and cancelled trains for passengers. It said its assessment following detailed and extensive analysis is that the capacity and performance of the southern section of the West Coast Main Line has not materially changed since it rejected a similar application by Lumo last year. An external review commissioned by ORR also supported this conclusion.
